text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Rebels soften stand on hostages: Direct talks with government lead Peruvian guerrillas to adopt more conciliatory tone.
- Police struggle to catch unsafe rigs: Many trucks fail roadside tests.
- Snow closes B.C. cities: Storm worst in 75 years.
- Doug Young won't rush to fill top military post: Defence Minister concedes Canadian Forces' leadership problems are serious.
- Muslim extremists kill 28 in Algeria: Algiers passes new weapons-control legislation in response to village massacre.
- From shop floor to computer room: The 100-year walk from the foundry to the microprocessor was complicated, but not accidental.
- Trade tops Ottawa's agenda: With 1997 an election year, cultivating Asia-Pacific markets seen as source for jobs.
- U.S. pension battle looms: Wall Street stands to make big gains.
- Biotech firm tries new prescription: Using a novel approach, Scotia Holdings aims to be a major pharmaceutical player.
- Vehicle glut spells gloom for world's auto makers.
- Top Arakis staffers quit: Three executives leave controversial Calgary oil and gas firm whose US$1 billion Sudan oil project has had a checkered past.
- Business caught in Ottawa's inter-ministry shootout.
